properties.name: Minnipa (closed)
properties.notes: Named closed in Viterra's June 2019 rationalisation of 17 up-country sites, six of them on EP. Primary source: Alisha Fogden, 'SILO SLASH: 17 Viterra grain sites to close', Stock Journal, 6 Jun 2019 (upd. 7 Jun 2019), and 'Croppers angry as upper EP silos take a hit', Stock Journal, 6 Jun 2019 - 'The sites of Minnipa, Kyancutta, Cungena, Waddikee, Kielpa and Wharminda have been closed.' The Farm Online item is the 7 Jun 2019 syndication of the first ('This story first appeared on Stock Journal') and is listed as a reprint, not as an independent outlet. Viterra's stated reasons, per operations manager Michael Hill: average truck size up 30 per cent since 2010 with bigger trucks going to bigger sites; quality-management and food-safety requirements; the closed sites were 'less than 2pc of total receivals (based on a five-year average)'. One of only TWO of the six that were operating the year before: 'six sites open last year at Minnipa, Kyancutta, Brinkworth, Paskeville, Millicent and Walpeup in Vic would not play a future role in the Viterra network'. NO PUBLISHED SOURCE ATTRIBUTES THE 2019 CLOSURES TO THE MAY 2019 EP RAIL SHUTDOWN. Neither Stock Journal story gives rail as a cause; 'freight redirection' survives only in a URL slug and appears nowhere in either body. Rail is mentioned once across both stories, by Minnipa cropper Matt Cook, about a different and earlier local closure. Any rail link is this project's inference and must be labelled as one. (Corrected 2026-08-31: this note previously read 'Closed in Viterra's 2019 network rationalisation after EP rail shutdown'. The trailing clause was unsourced and is withdrawn.)
properties.operating_seasons_source: operator weekly harvest reports (data/processed/receivals_notes.jsonl); positive evidence only - absence of a mention is NOT evidence of closure

properties.name: Cungena (closed)
properties.notes: Named closed in Viterra's June 2019 rationalisation of 17 up-country sites, six of them on EP. Primary source: Alisha Fogden, 'SILO SLASH: 17 Viterra grain sites to close', Stock Journal, 6 Jun 2019 (upd. 7 Jun 2019), and 'Croppers angry as upper EP silos take a hit', Stock Journal, 6 Jun 2019 - 'The sites of Minnipa, Kyancutta, Cungena, Waddikee, Kielpa and Wharminda have been closed.' The Farm Online item is the 7 Jun 2019 syndication of the first ('This story first appeared on Stock Journal') and is listed as a reprint, not as an independent outlet. Viterra's stated reasons, per operations manager Michael Hill: average truck size up 30 per cent since 2010 with bigger trucks going to bigger sites; quality-management and food-safety requirements; the closed sites were 'less than 2pc of total receivals (based on a five-year average)'. NOT operating the year before: it is in the group of 11 'that were not open the year prior' that 'would also be closed permanently'. A pre-2019 network state that counts it as open overstates the 2018/19 network. NO PUBLISHED SOURCE ATTRIBUTES THE 2019 CLOSURES TO THE MAY 2019 EP RAIL SHUTDOWN. Neither Stock Journal story gives rail as a cause; 'freight redirection' survives only in a URL slug and appears nowhere in either body. Rail is mentioned once across both stories, by Minnipa cropper Matt Cook, about a different and earlier local closure. Any rail link is this project's inference and must be labelled as one. CONTRADICTED, AND THE CONTRADICTION IS UNRESOLVED: Viterra's own weekly harvest report for the week ending 13 Nov 2022 names Cungena among sites that 'received their first new season deliveries'. Both sources are published and neither is retracted. What they jointly support is that it was closed in June 2019 and described as permanent, that it nonetheless took first new-season deliveries in 2022/23, and that no published evidence has it operating in any other season. The bare 'closed permanently 2019' tag this note used to carry is wrong as written; the defensible statement is a season range. See data/SOURCES.md 'cungena-status-contradiction'. Corrected 2026-08-31.

properties.name: Wharminda (closed)
properties.notes: Named closed in Viterra's June 2019 rationalisation of 17 up-country sites, six of them on EP. Primary source: Alisha Fogden, 'SILO SLASH: 17 Viterra grain sites to close', Stock Journal, 6 Jun 2019 (upd. 7 Jun 2019), and 'Croppers angry as upper EP silos take a hit', Stock Journal, 6 Jun 2019 - 'The sites of Minnipa, Kyancutta, Cungena, Waddikee, Kielpa and Wharminda have been closed.' The Farm Online item is the 7 Jun 2019 syndication of the first ('This story first appeared on Stock Journal') and is listed as a reprint, not as an independent outlet. Viterra's stated reasons, per operations manager Michael Hill: average truck size up 30 per cent since 2010 with bigger trucks going to bigger sites; quality-management and food-safety requirements; the closed sites were 'less than 2pc of total receivals (based on a five-year average)'. NOT operating the year before: it is in the group of 11 'that were not open the year prior' that 'would also be closed permanently'. A pre-2019 network state that counts it as open overstates the 2018/19 network. NO PUBLISHED SOURCE ATTRIBUTES THE 2019 CLOSURES TO THE MAY 2019 EP RAIL SHUTDOWN. Named once in ten seasons of the operator's weekly reports, in 2016/17.
